summary: Risk-first ordering with a walking skeleton. Risk ranking (highest first) and why each item sits where it does: R1 toolchain and dependency install (npm ci on a committed lockfile, re2-wasm and SDK major pins, tsc over non-empty src, ESLint ban rules proven by probes) is T001 because every later task fails if it fails. R2 cross-component integration of MCP stdio server, job registry, real worker thread and polled get_scan_status, with a fake OSV transport, is T002 (walking skeleton, design 3.2/3.3/4.1/6), reached right after the toolchain so integration errors surface before detailed logic exists; later tasks keep its file names and tool contract and replace its internals (T045, T047, T059; job.stubResult is preserved through T045-T046 and removed in T047). R3 cancel/timeout concurrency is T003-T005 (error catalogue and transition table, drain rows and first-wins, cancel controller on an injectable fake clock and stub worker): it needs only constants.ts from T001 and is the hardest semantics. R4 network confinement and the OSV client on a fake transport is T006; real HTTP is never exercised by tests. R5 constants tests T007-T010 are cheap guards over src/constants.ts and carry no integration risk, so they sit behind R1-R4. R6 pure logic follows in dependency order: scoring (T011-T012), secrets (T013-T017, G3), path and output-dir security (T018-T021), finding identity/dedupe/truncation (T022-T024, G2), walker/reader (T025-T028), rules and scanners (T029-T039), contracts and envelope (T040-T044), job manager and execution (T045-T048), get_findings, writer and reports (T049-T056), list_scanners and the full 6-tool server (T057-T059), fixtures and e2e (T060-T063) and a traceability gate (T064) over goals G1-G6, section 9 failure modes (every F-id, cited in test titles) and section 11 trade-offs. The chain is linear on purpose: the implement loop is sequential and needs a unique deterministic order, so each task depends on its immediate predecessor (T001 -> T002 -> ... -> T064, contiguous ids). Risk order is encoded by position: the three riskiest unknowns (toolchain, stdio+worker integration, cancel/timeout) occupy positions 1, 2 and 3-5. Rollback/partial-state policy: every task is additive or an in-place extension (shared files such as src/scanners/secret.ts, src/security/paths.ts, rules/rules.json, schemas/tools.json, src/jobs/jobManager.ts, src/jobs/worker.ts, src/server.ts are extended, never replaced wholesale) and each intent states what exists, what is absent and which verify command proves green; the full-suite command (tsc --noEmit plus node --import tsx --test test/*.test.ts) is a verify of nearly every task from T002, so the project can stop after any task in a consistent state. From T002 the engine is reachable over stdio with two tools; the full 6-tool contract is served from T059. Verify-command policy: all commands run from the repo root in a POSIX shell (Git Bash/sh); the test glob test/*.test.ts is expanded by that shell (node --test with a directory argument does not discover .ts tests). Negative checks are plain grep/eslint/script commands with expect_exit_code 1 (grep: 1 = no match, 2 = error fails), each paired with a temp-tree fixture proof that the pattern exits 0 on forbidden snippets and 1 on clean code. Headings with no implementation of their own: none; the title is covered by T001, "1. Goals / non-goals" by T062-T064; out-of-scope items are non-goals.
